inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL scalar INTERVAL expression assigns a one-based bracket index by comparing a value against ordered numeric thresholds.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored shipment SLA report. Fixed decimal transit durations are bracketed by ordered day thresholds and translated into labels through CASE; exact boundary values, a below-threshold value, and a NULL value are retained to exercise comparison edges. The source test data and function bundle are not copied.

fixture_notes: Thresholds are 3, 7, 14, 30, and 60 days. Values below the first threshold return bracket 0; exact boundaries advance to the next bracket; NULL input returns MariaDB's -1 bracket index and is retained in the report.
determinism_notes: All shipment IDs, durations, thresholds, and labels are fixed; output is ordered by the unique shipment ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE shipment_sla (shipment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, transit_days DECIMAL(6,2) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT shipment_id, transit_days, INTERVAL(transit_days, 3, 7, 14, 30, 60) AS bracket_index, CASE INTERVAL(transit_days, 3, 7, 14, 30, 60) WHEN 0 THEN 'under-3' WHEN 1 THEN '3-to-6' WHEN 2 THEN '7-to-13' WHEN 3 THEN '14-to-29' WHEN 4 THEN '30-to-59' ELSE '60-plus' END AS sla_band FROM shipment_sla ORDER BY shipment_id
